name: Neon
tagline: Serverless Postgres with copy-on-write branching and scale-to-zero, now part of Databricks.
description: Neon is a serverless PostgreSQL service that splits Postgres into stateless compute and a custom storage layer (safekeepers for the WAL, pageservers backed by object storage). That design enables instant copy-on-write branches of a whole database, point-in-time restore inside a history window, and computes that autoscale and suspend to zero when idle. It became the default Postgres for preview environments, AI app builders and agent-created databases. Databricks acquired Neon in 2025 and its technology now also underpins Databricks Lakebase. The free plan remains generous, and paid plans are purely usage-based, so it is a strong fit for many small or bursty databases; cold starts and shared-storage latency make it less ideal for steady, latency-critical OLTP.

pricing.notes: Free plan: 100 CU-hours and 1 GB storage per project, up to 2 CU autoscaling, scale-to-zero after 5 minutes. Scale plan $0.222/CU-hour; storage $0.35/GB-month.

scale.notes: Autoscaling single-writer compute with read replicas sharing storage; projects are pinned to one region.

strengths: Instant copy-on-write branches for preview environments, tests and agents
Scale-to-zero and autoscaling make thousands of small databases cheap
Time-travel queries and instant restore within the history window
Serverless HTTP/WebSocket driver works from edge runtimes
Real Postgres with common extensions (pgvector, PostGIS)
weaknesses: Cold starts after suspend add latency to the first query
Storage over network/object storage is slower than local NVMe for heavy OLTP
Product roadmap now tied to Databricks priorities; public repo activity has slowed
useCases: AI app builders and agents provisioning databases on demand
SaaS with many small, mostly idle tenant databases
Serverless and edge apps on Vercel or Cloudflare
notIdealFor: Steady high-throughput OLTP with strict latency SLOs
